kill_fact: The catalyst survives the kill-check but the entry-timing argument does not. The bull's stated reason to buy now rather than wait is that the two thesis-breakers -- an FDA advisory committee being called, or a three-month extension of the review clock -- 'get less likely with every week that passes this late in a standard review.' That is wrong on the clock. The NDA was accepted 9 March 2026 for a 22 December 2026 action date; as of 27 July 2026 roughly five of about nine and a half review months are still to run. Advisory committee meetings are noticed in the Federal Register typically 30 to 60 days ahead, which puts the announcement window in October and November, entirely in the future. Three-month extensions triggered by a major amendment are likewise issued late in the review. Both risks the bull books as 'quiet positives' sit almost wholly ahead of the position, not behind it. The absence of either today carries close to no information, so the argument against simply waiting for the 11 August results and the autumn payer datapoints collapses. Everything else holds: the 22 December 2026 target action date is confirmed from the company's own filing-acceptance release and reconfirmed in its first-quarter results; the financing structure, the senior secured ranking and the Tanabe milestone tail are confirmed to the dollar; the spread has not closed, with the shares at $26.71 against the bull's own approval-resolved $38. The soft floor is a genuine weakness but it is disclosed, quantified and sized for by the bull rather than hidden, so it is not a disqualifier.
corrections: 1. MATERIAL -- entry timing. Strike the claim that the absence of an advisory committee or a clock extension 'this late in a standard review' is meaningfully reassuring, and strike the conclusion that entering now beats waiting. Roughly five of about nine and a half review months remain; the announcement window for both events is ahead, not behind. The forcing function and the December date are untouched -- only the argument for immediate entry fails. 2. MATERIAL -- the chronic kidney disease evidence is understated, and it cuts in the bull's favour. The dossier calls the kidney work 'a post-hoc subgroup analysis' and values the pipeline beyond lorundrostat-in-hypertension at 'effectively nil.' That is wrong. Explore-CKD (NCT06150924) is a dedicated randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled two-by-two crossover Phase 2 that MET its primary endpoint on 17 June 2025: at 25 mg, a 9.3 mmHg reduction in automated office systolic blood pressure (7.5 mmHg placebo-adjusted, p=0.0024) at four weeks and a 31% reduction in spot urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (p<0.0001). Re-verified independently against the company's 17 June 2025 release and its Form 8-K exhibit 99.1 (SEC accession 0001933414-25-000070). Decisively, the background therapy in that trial ALREADY INCLUDED an SGLT2 inhibitor plus an ACE inhibitor or ARB, in subjects with eGFR at or above 30 and UACR of 200-5,000 mg/g. That directly refutes the bear's specific claim that lorundrostat is 'structurally disadvantaged in the kidney-disease and SGLT2-combination opportunity' -- the drug has prospective, placebo-controlled, statistically significant data ON TOP OF an SGLT2 inhibitor, which is the exact combination the bear asserts it loses. The 30 May 2026 ESH presentation was separately a post-hoc analysis of Launch-HTN; the dossier conflated the two and omitted the prospective trial. The rejection-branch residual value of about $0.6 billion and the 'no differentiation versus baxdrostat' concession should both be re-underwritten against a real prospective dataset. 3. MATERIAL -- ex-United States optionality is encumbered. The 2 June 2026 fourth amendment grants Mineralys an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual licence, but the parties' planned follow-on termination agreement expressly PRESERVES Tanabe's right of first negotiation for Japan. The $0.3 billion of 'ex-United States and partnering optionality' in the sum-of-parts is therefore not unencumbered and should be haircut. 4. MINOR -- baxdrostat approval date. Baxfendy was approved in the United States on 18 MAY 2026, not 15 May 2026. Cited four times in the dossier; the fact that the FDA has blessed the mechanism is unaffected. 5. MINOR -- Explore-OSA and NDA acceptance were announced on 9 MARCH 2026, not 10 March 2026. 6. MINOR -- short interest framing is stale. The level is confirmed: 9.55 million shares, 14.44% of a 66.16 million free float. But the 'growing one-sided bet' framing is out of date -- the position fell from 11.10 million shares the prior month, so shorts are already covering and part of the demand-into-December the bull banks on has been consumed. 7. MINOR -- the 11 August 2026 second-quarter date is an estimate, not an announced date. The company has issued no press release since 14 June 2026 and has not scheduled its second-quarter call. 8. CONFIRMED, NO CHANGE -- the floor arithmetic. Cash and investments of $646.1 million at 31 March 2026, plus $150.0 million gross from 5,660,378 shares at $26.50, plus the $100 million first tranche, less the $200 million Tanabe upfront, gives roughly $696 million before second-quarter burn and about $650 million after it; net of the senior secured tranche that is roughly $550 million, or about $6.2 a share on 88.16 million shares. The dossier's $640 million gross, $540 million net and $6.15 a share are sound. The Pharmakon facility is confirmed senior secured, up to $500 million, $100 million funded at closing, maturing June 2031, at SOFR with a 3.25% floor plus a 5.50% margin, and the Tanabe milestone tail is confirmed at up to $265 million. The $13 rejection floor remains an estimate rather than a contractual backstop -- correctly disclosed, and it must stay the binding constraint on size. 9. MINOR -- unsourced inference in the floor construction, and it cuts FOR the bull. The dossier asserts three times that the remaining three Pharmakon tranches 'carry drawdown conditions the company would likely fail in a rejection scenario.' The 3 June 2026 primary release says only that further tranches are 'subject to customary conditions' and does NOT name FDA approval of lorundrostat as a drawdown condition. Treat the approval-contingency as an assumption rather than a documented term unless the loan agreement exhibit says otherwise; the rejection-branch floor may be marginally less bad than the bear draws it. 10. MINOR -- stale price anchor. The $26.71 in the dossier is the prior close; the shares last traded $27.21. Recomputed, the payoff is +39.7% to the $38 approval-resolved target against -52.2% to the $13 floor, and the expected value is +30.5% rather than +33%. Shape and conclusion unchanged, and the spread is emphatically still open. 11. MINOR -- analyst marks are only partly verifiable. Only the Goldman Sachs $42 (Richard Law, 4 June 2026) was independently confirmed from a primary attribution; the Guggenheim $48, LifeSci Capital $54 and H.C. Wainwright $56 marks could not be verified, and published aggregate consensus reads nearer $51 than the dossier's $49. This is a sanity-check number rather than a valuation input, so nothing in the sum-of-parts moves -- but the dossier should not present the four-broker fan as verified.
